title: A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity
text: McCulloch and Pitts, Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics: the neuron as a threshold unit.

title: The Organization of Behavior
text: Hebb's book: cells that fire together wire together, a rule for learning.

title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
text: Turing, Mind: the imitation game, and machines that learn.

title: SNARC
text: Minsky and Edmonds build a learning machine of about 40 Hebb synapses from vacuum tubes and motors.

title: Samuel's checkers program
text: Arthur Samuel's program for the IBM 701 plays checkers, and later learns to play it better.

title: The Dartmouth workshop
text: McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon name the field: artificial intelligence.

title: Lloyd's algorithm
text: Stuart Lloyd's Bell Labs memo: quantize by alternating nearest centers and means, the k-means algorithm. Published in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, March 1982.

title: The perceptron
text: Rosenblatt, Psychological Review: a neuron whose weights are learned.

title: Some studies in machine learning using the game of checkers
text: Samuel, IBM Journal of Research and Development: a program that learns from its games, and the words machine learning.

title: Adaptive switching circuits
text: Widrow and Hoff, IRE WESCON: ADALINE, trained by the least-mean-squares rule.

title: Cybernetic predicting devices
text: Ivakhnenko and Lapa: deep networks of polynomial units, grown and trained layer by layer (the group method of data handling).

title: Nearest neighbor pattern classification
text: Cover and Hart, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory: label a point as its nearest known neighbor.

title: Some methods for classification and analysis of multivariate observations
text: MacQueen, Fifth Berkeley Symposium: the name k-means.

title: Perceptrons
text: Minsky and Papert's book: what one layer cannot learn.

title: Reverse-mode differentiation
text: Linnainmaa's master's thesis, Helsinki: the derivative of a whole computation, carried backward, the algorithm under backpropagation (in English: BIT, 1976).

title: The Lighthill report
text: Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey, for the UK Science Research Council; funding is cut, the first AI winter.

title: Beyond regression
text: Werbos's Harvard thesis: backpropagation through a network, to train it.

title: Neocognitron
text: Fukushima, Biological Cybernetics: layers of local feature detectors and pooling, the CNN's forerunner.

title: Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities
text: Hopfield, PNAS: a network whose energy falls to stored memories.

title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors
text: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams, Nature: backpropagation trains hidden layers.

title: Backpropagation applied to handwritten zip code recognition
text: LeCun et al., Neural Computation: a convolutional network learns to read digits.

title: Word association norms, mutual information, and lexicography
text: Church and Hanks, Computational Linguistics: words that keep company, measured by mutual information.

title: Adaptive mixtures of local experts
text: Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan and Hinton, Neural Computation: a gate learns which expert answers.

title: TD-Gammon
text: Tesauro, Machine Learning: a network taught by temporal differences, playing itself, plays backgammon near the best humans.

title: Support-vector networks
text: Cortes and Vapnik, Machine Learning: the widest margin between two classes.

title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
text: IBM's chess machine wins a six-game match against the world champion.

title: Long short-term memory
text: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber, Neural Computation: a recurrent network that remembers.

title: Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition
text: LeCun, Bottou, Bengio and Haffner, Proceedings of the IEEE: LeNet-5, and the MNIST digits.

title: Random forests
text: Breiman, Machine Learning: many trees, each on a random sample, voting.

title: A fast learning algorithm for deep belief nets
text: Hinton, Osindero and Teh, Neural Computation: deep networks pre-trained a layer at a time.

title: ImageNet: a large-scale hierarchical image database
text: Deng, Dong, Socher, Li, Li and Fei-Fei, CVPR: millions of labeled pictures.

title: Rectified linear units improve restricted Boltzmann machines
text: Nair and Hinton, ICML: the ReLU, max(0, x).

title: Watson wins Jeopardy!
text: IBM's question-answering system beats Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter on television.

title: ImageNet classification with deep convolutional neural networks
text: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton (AlexNet), NeurIPS: GPUs, ReLU and dropout.

title: Efficient estimation of word representations in vector space
text: Mikolov, Chen, Corrado and Dean: word2vec, a word as a vector that its neighbors predict.

title: Auto-encoding variational Bayes
text: Kingma and Welling: the variational autoencoder.

title: Generative adversarial networks
text: Goodfellow et al.: a generator and a discriminator trained against each other.

title: Dropout: a simple way to prevent neural networks from overfitting
text: Srivastava, Hinton, Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Salakhutdinov, JMLR: drop units at random while training.

title: Neural machine translation by jointly learning to align and translate
text: Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio: attention, a decoder that looks back at every input word.

title: Adam: a method for stochastic optimization
text: Kingma and Ba: a step size for every weight.

title: Batch normalization
text: Ioffe and Szegedy: normalize each layer's inputs over the batch.

title: Deep unsupervised learning using nonequilibrium thermodynamics
text: Sohl-Dickstein, Weiss, Maheswaranathan and Ganguli: the first diffusion model.

title: Deep residual learning for image recognition
text: He, Zhang, Ren and Sun: ResNet, layers that learn what to add to their input.

title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
text: DeepMind's Go program wins four games of five.

title: Ternary weight networks
text: Li and Liu: weights of -1, 0 and +1 times a scale.

title: Outrageously large neural networks: the sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer
text: Shazeer et al.: thousands of experts, a few chosen for each token.

title: Attention is all you need
text: Vaswani et al.: the Transformer.

title: Proximal policy optimization algorithms
text: Schulman et al.: PPO, policy steps clipped to stay near the last policy.

title: AlphaGo Zero
text: Silver et al., Nature: Go learned from self-play alone, no human games.

title: World models
text: Ha and Schmidhuber: an agent that learns a model of its world and trains inside its dream.

title: Improving language understanding by generative pre-training
text: Radford, Narasimhan, Salimans and Sutskever, OpenAI: GPT, a Transformer pre-trained to predict the next word.

title: BERT
text: Devlin et al.: a Transformer pre-trained by filling in masked words.

title: Language models are unsupervised multitask learners
text: Radford et al., OpenAI: GPT-2.

title: Scaling laws for neural language models
text: Kaplan et al.: loss falls as a power of size, data and compute.

title: GLU variants improve Transformer
text: Shazeer: gated feed-forward layers, SwiGLU among them.

title: Language models are few-shot learners
text: Brown et al.: GPT-3.

title: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models
text: Ho, Jain and Abbeel: pictures from noise, a step at a time.

title: An image is worth 16x16 words
text: Dosovitskiy et al.: the Vision Transformer, a picture read as patches.

title: Switch Transformers
text: Fedus, Zoph and Shazeer: route each token to a single expert, and scale to a trillion weights.

title: Learning transferable visual models from natural language supervision
text: Radford et al.: CLIP, pictures and captions embedded in one space.

title: LoRA: low-rank adaptation of large language models
text: Hu et al.: fine-tune a frozen matrix through two thin ones.

title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
text: Jumper et al., Nature: AlphaFold 2 predicts how proteins fold.

title: High-resolution image synthesis with latent diffusion models
text: Rombach, Blattmann, Lorenz, Esser and Ommer: diffusion in a compressed space, Stable Diffusion's method.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
text: Ouyang et al.: InstructGPT, fine-tuned on what people prefer.

title: ChatGPT
text: OpenAI's chat model, released to the public.

title: LLaMA: open and efficient foundation language models
text: Touvron et al.: open weights, trained on public data.

title: QLoRA
text: Dettmers et al.: LoRA on a base quantized to 4 bits.

title: Direct preference optimization
text: Rafailov et al.: DPO, learn from preferred answers with no reward model.

title: LoRA-FA
text: Zhang, Zhang, Shi, Chu and Li: LoRA with its down projection frozen, to save activations' memory.

title: VeRA: vector-based random matrix adaptation
text: Kopiczko, Blankevoort and Asano: frozen random matrices, two trained vectors.

title: BitNet: scaling 1-bit Transformers for large language models
text: Wang et al.: weights of one bit, trained so from the start.

title: Mixtral 8x7B
text: Mistral AI releases an open mixture of experts: eight experts, two per token.

title: Mixtral of experts
text: Jiang et al.: the paper on Mixtral 8x7B.

title: The era of 1-bit LLMs
text: Ma et al.: BitNet b1.58, every weight -1, 0 or +1.

title: The Nobel Prize in Physics
text: To Hopfield and Hinton, for discoveries that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks.

title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry
text: To Baker, for computational protein design, and to Hassabis and Jumper, for AlphaFold's protein structure prediction.

title: DeepSeek-V3 technical report
text: DeepSeek-AI: a mixture of experts of 671 billion weights, 37 billion used per token.

title: DeepSeek-R1
text: DeepSeek-AI: reasoning learned by reinforcement learning; in Nature, September 2025.

title: The Turing Award for reinforcement learning
text: To Barto and Sutton, for its conceptual and algorithmic foundations.

title: Gold at the Mathematical Olympiad
text: Google DeepMind's Gemini Deep Think solves five of six IMO problems in natural language, a gold medal's score.

title: X_eTaL
text: The eXperimental Extensible Typed Array Language begins: a typed array language that runs at the command line and in the browser.

title: X_eTaL v0.1.0
text: X_eTaL's first release, with macro libraries.

title: X_eTaL-ML
text: This repository: machine learning in X_eTaL, its demos live in the browser and the libraries they are built from.
